findings.problem: The default pytest.mark.timeout(900) uses pytest-timeout's default func_only=False, so it also covers the setup phase of the first e2e test. findings.failure_scenario: First `make test-e2e` on a clean Windows host or uncached CI, where `up -d --build` of ~11 images plus the health waits exceeds 15 min. pytest-timeout fires during e2e_stack setup. findings.problem: The function's docstring says parse_provision_output errors "name the line keys only", and its test says it "never echoes the token". In fact the error prints everything before the first '=' of every stdout line. A line with no '=' goes in whole, and so does a line that uses ':' as its separator. Either one can put the one-time set-password token into the ValueError. That error then reaches the HopFailure message and the CI log.
findings.failure_scenario: The IF-08 CLI (scripts.provision_clinician) does not exist yet. Suppose it, or anything it imports, writes a structlog JSON line to stdout that holds the link, such as {"event":"account_setup_link_issued","link":"http://x/account-setup/TOKEN"}. Or suppose it prints 'set_password_url: http://x/account-setup/TOKEN'. Then keys = [<whole line>, ...] and the ValueError text holds the token. I ran a scratch probe of both shapes and the token was echoed each time (True). The existing test only covers lines that follow the key=value form.
findings.fix: Print only keys that match ^[a-z_]+$, and replace anything else with a placeholder such as '<unexpected line>'. Or report only the line count and the expected keys. Add the JSON-line and colon-separator cases to test_mvp_039_provision_output_must_be_exactly_two_lines_and_never_echoes_the_token.

findings.problem: _expect copies the first 300 characters of the response body into the AssertionError, which becomes the HopFailure message and the CI log. FastAPI 0.133 with pydantic 2.13 (both locked) echoes request input in its default 422 body, and user-service registers no RequestValidationError handler. So a schema mismatch on account-setup, register or login puts the one-time account-setup token and the generated password into the failure text. The same happens if login returns an unexpected 2xx whose body holds tokens.
findings.failure_scenario: provision_clinician POSTs {token, new_password} to /api/v1/users/account-setup. That route does not exist yet (IF-08/IF-17). If it lands expecting a field named 'password', FastAPI returns 422 with detail[0].input = {"token": "<one-time token>", "new_password": "<pw>"}. That body is inside the first 300 characters, so the clinician's set-password token and password are printed in the HopFailure.
findings.fix: Do not echo the body for auth flows. Report the status and, for a JSON error, only detail[*].type and detail[*].loc. Or pass the request's sensitive values to _scrub before formatting the body.
findings.evidence: e2e.py:785-787 raises AssertionError(f"{what}: HTTP {response.status_code} (expected {statuses}): {response.text[:300]}"). It is used at lines 800, 815, 819, 847 and 850. requirements.lock pins fastapi==0.133.0 and pydantic==2.13.4. A Grep of services/user-service finds no RequestValidationError handler.

findings.problem: run_dir comes from SOLACE_E2E_RUN_DIR or the ps1 -RunDir, and nothing validates it. _start calls shutil.rmtree on it unconditionally before it generates anything, and _teardown (stop_stack, 'down') deletes it again. Neither checks that the directory is one the harness created, for example that it holds e2e.env or a marker. This skips the generator's own refuse-to-overwrite-without---rotate guard and can delete an arbitrary operator directory.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator reads 'RunDir' as a parent directory and runs '.\scripts\test\e2e_stack.ps1 down -RunDir D:\tmp', or sets SOLACE_E2E_RUN_DIR=D:\tmp\mvp-exec before a pytest run. _teardown or _start then runs shutil.rmtree('D:\tmp...') and deletes the whole tree, including the mvp-exec state.
findings.fix: Before any rmtree, require that the directory is empty or holds the harness's e2e.env (or a marker file the generator writes). Otherwise raise. Or always use a project-named subdirectory under the configured base.
findings.evidence: e2e.py:743-747: if not (config.reuse and config.env_file.is_file()): _remove_project(config); if config.run_dir.exists(): shutil.rmtree(config.run_dir). e2e.py:649-650 does the same in _teardown. StackConfig.from_env (188-191) and __post_init__ (172-173) accept any path.

That body is inside the first 300 characters, so the clinician's set-password token and password are printed in the HopFailure.
verified.fix: Do not echo the body for auth flows. Report the status and, for a JSON error, only detail[*].type and detail[*].loc. Or pass the request's sensitive values to _scrub before formatting the body.
verified.evidence: e2e.py:785-787 raises AssertionError(f"{what}: HTTP {response.status_code} (expected {statuses}): {response.text[:300]}"). It is used at lines 800, 815, 819, 847 and 850. requirements.lock pins fastapi==0.133.0 and pydantic==2.13.4. A Grep of services/user-service finds no RequestValidationError handler.

votes.reason: The code at e2e.py:785-787 puts response.text[:300] into the AssertionError with no _scrub. _scrub exists but is not applied here. user-service registers only TokenExpiredError, TokenInvalidError, ValueError and Exception handlers (main.py:605-632), so FastAPI's default RequestValidationError handler still returns the 422 body. RequestValidationError is not a ValueError subclass, so the ValueError handler does not catch it. For a missing-field error pydantic puts the whole request dict in "input", and that dict sits well within the first 300 characters. A schema mismatch on account-setup, register or login would therefore print the one-time token and generated password into the failure text and CI log. This is conditional: today the account-setup route returns 404, which leaks nothing. The secrets are also ephemeral, per-run test credentials. Minor severity is appropriate. I did not run pytest or render any compose config, because the code reading was enough.

findings.problem: On POSIX, _write_certs chmods every produced file to 0600, including e2e-ca.crt, mailpit.crt, postgres-ca.crt and server.crt. scripts/db/gen_certs.py deliberately writes the CAs and certs as 0644 and only the keys as 0600. Compose file-secrets in non-swarm mode are plain bind mounts that keep the host owner and mode. The app images run as appuser (uid 1000), and so does the migrate job.
findings.failure_scenario: On a Linux host whose uid is not 1000 (a GitHub-hosted runner is uid 1001), /run/secrets/postgres-ca.crt and /run/secrets/e2e-ca.crt are 0600 and owned by another uid. The app services and migrate cannot read the CA. In the strict profile, POSTGRES_SSL verify-full and SSL_CERT_FILE for mailpit STARTTLS then fail, so stack_up fails on CI. The Windows run cannot show this, and tests/scripts/test_mvp_039_gen_e2e_env.py asserts no file modes.
findings.fix: Keep the gen_certs modes: chmod 0644 for *.crt and 0600 only for *.key (or skip the second chmod pass for the certs). Add a POSIX-only test that asserts e2e-ca.crt and postgres-ca.crt are world-readable.
findings.evidence: gen_e2e_env.py lines 285-286 call _restrict_file (os.chmod 0o600 when os.name != 'nt') on all names from _write_certs. gen_certs.py line 54 sets _FILE_MODES = {CA_FILE: 0o644, CERT_FILE: 0o644, KEY_FILE: 0o600}. The service Dockerfiles use USER appuser with uid 1000. docker-compose.prod.yml mounts postgres-ca.crt into every client.

votes.reason: The code matches the finding. gen_e2e_env.py lines 285-286 call _restrict_file, which does os.chmod 0o600 on POSIX, for every name returned by _write_certs. That list includes mailpit.crt and, in the strict profile, the Postgres CA and server certs. e2e-ca.crt is among the mailpit files, so it is included too. scripts/db/gen_certs.py sets _FILE_MODES to 0o644 for the CA and cert files and 0o600 only for keys, so this pass narrows them on purpose-built 0644 files. The generator writes only these cert files into secrets/. Passwords go into e2e.env, so the certs are the only files the containers read from the secrets directory. The overlay mounts e2e-ca.crt as a compose file secret on all nine app services, and the service Dockerfiles use USER appuser. Non-swarm file secrets are bind mounts that keep the host owner and mode. A 0600 CA owned by a host uid other than the container's (a GitHub runner is uid 1001) is therefore unreadable inside the container. That breaks the CA trust the strict profile needs. I did not confirm appuser's uid is 1000 or run the stack. The failure also depends on the CI host uid differing from the container uid, so it is conditional. A developer host with uid 1000 would not hit it. The fix is simple (0644 for *.crt, 0600 for keys), and 'important' is reasonable for a CI-only break.

The brief (line 52) says the generator restricts permissions and, on POSIX, uses "modes 700/600". gen_e2e_env.py does exactly that: 0700 on the directory and 0600 on files. The implementer's report (WS-05.4-report.md, item 4 under part 1b) records this risk, in the same words as the finding: compose file secrets keep the host uid and mode, so 0600 may block non-root container users on Linux CI. It marks this "Verify on Linux in part 2". The behaviour was therefore specified by the brief and the risk was already flagged and deferred. It is a known follow-up for part 2, whose live self-test cannot run now anyway. It is not an unnoticed part 1 defect, and "important" overstates it. I did not check whether the 0600 modes actually fail on a Linux host. Nothing in this lens settles that, so part 2 still needs to test it.

The code confirms the claim. gen_e2e_env.py lines 285-286 call _restrict_file on every cert name, including the CA certs (e2e-ca.crt, mailpit.crt, postgres-ca.crt, server.crt). Non-swarm compose file secrets are bind mounts that keep the host owner and mode, and the app images run as a non-root appuser (uid 1000, per the finding; I did not re-check the Dockerfiles). A Linux CI runner with a different uid, such as 1001, would therefore leave the CA unreadable inside the containers. This is a real bug on the path the harness is built for (Linux CI), and it breaks stack_up in the strict profile. Important is the right severity: the failure is loud and test-only, and the fix is small (0644 for *.crt, 0600 for keys). I did not run the tests or inspect the generated file modes.
